translations.text: This blessed father of ours, John, came from the land of Mesopotamia, from the region of Antioch.
Under the guidance of the Holy Spirit he came to this land of Kartli, near the holy mother-city of Mtskheta.
This holy and God-clothed man had begun his life as a monk in his own land.
He lived in all humility and struggle, in fasting and vigils, and in tears and prayers to God, as it says:
"Knock and it will be opened to you; ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find."
This blessed man also found grace before God, and he saw what was far off as if it were near. And he shone forth like a star.
And the mighty works and wonders that he performed through God upon diseases of many and various kinds multiplied.
But he left the place where he was living and went away into the far desert, for he was fleeing this vain glory.
And he found a cave in that desert and settled in it with his disciples. And for a long time no one knew of that place.
From time to time he would send one of the disciples to fetch food, and in this way he lived in secret.
But God revealed his servant once again, as it says: "Whoever humbles himself will be exalted."
And when it became known where he was living, people brought the sick and the possessed to him on litters, and all were healed by the power of God and by the prayers of our holy father John.
Many are the miracles that are recorded there.
But since he was fleeing the honors of the world, he resolved to go abroad as a stranger, to where no report of him was heard.
And as he was resolving this, he said to his disciples: "I am going to a foreign land, but you stay here and pray for me too."
But they said to him: "As the Lord lives, we will not let you go alone; we too will come, so that we may not be deprived of the spring
from which we drink through you, for you are the guide of our souls, and through your graces we await mercy from God."
So bound together were they by spiritual love.
And they set out from their own land, and under the guidance of the Holy Spirit they arrived at the city of Mtskheta.
And they went in and venerated the holy pillar that God, and not man, had raised up,
for neither the skill of the craftsmen nor the king himself, with a multitude of countless people, had been able to raise it for three days.
And they abandoned it and went away, taking all their machines with them, for they had lost hope.
But the cause of all good things, the enlightener and converter of the Georgians, the mother,
our apostle Nino, stood in prayer to God with fervent tears and asked for God's help in raising the pillar.
And as she was praying in this way, a power came from on high: the pillar was suspended up in the air, about one cubit high, and it stood by divine power,
At dawn King Mirian came with the Georgian people. When they saw this wondrous thing and glorious miracle, they were amazed.
And it came down slowly until it was set firmly on the foundation. And everyone who saw it and heard of it glorified God.
And a great many people were converted and were baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
The holy father John came before this Living Pillar.
And he raised his hands, lifted his eyes to heaven, shed tears and offered thanks to God.
And God showed him a mountain near Mtskheta and the Life-giving Cross, on the northern side, and told him to go up to the summit of that mountain.
And he crossed the Aragvi and went up to venerate the precious Cross. And when they had prayed there, he went up with his disciples onto that mountain.
And when he had looked around, he said to his disciples: "Here I will dwell, for this place pleases me."
God did this for these reasons: first, so that he might become an adornment to the churches and to the Georgian peoples round about.
And second, he settled in that place because the pagans had built a tower there, and demons had firmly made their dwelling there, and the pagans served them with the smoke of sacrifices.
And so that now, through the prayer of that holy elder, he might purify that place.
When this God-clothed father of ours, Saint John, had gone up the mountain, he began to pray to God and entreat him, and he mightily endured all the assaults of the demons.
And he wished to live in solitude, and he said to his disciples: "Children, why do you stand idle?
Do you not know that our Lord Jesus Christ sent us out for the benefit of this land and led us here, because this land is a new planting?
Therefore it is right that you go out, each one of you, and strengthen the brethren who have confessed Christ.
"And love nothing more than God, brothers. Keep away from luxury and gluttony,
for Adam's disobedience was born from luxury and food, and it rests on his offspring. It was this that drove him out of Paradise.
If he had kept that commandment of fasting, corruption and death would not have gained power over us,
although now, through Christ's becoming man, those of us who have now kept his commandment have become incorruptible.
"As for wine, there is no need even to speak of it, for it is not for monks, since the apostle Paul called it the root and agent of evil:
'And do not be drunk with wine, in which is filth.' It is a deadly poison and the mother of evil desires.
Do not touch it at all, for it lures us into eternal punishment. My brothers, always remember death and where we are going.
For this flesh is mortal and passing away, but the soul is immortal for ever. Let us strive here and now for our souls, for all this life belongs to tribulation, but the eternal life belongs to rest.
Let us be on guard for that terrible hour when the soul is separated from the body.
For great is the fear when they lead the soul away and pay it the reward for its deeds."
John taught his disciples much of this kind, and said to them: "Go forth and strengthen the flocks of Christ."
And he sent some of them to Kakheti, some to Kukheti, and others to the upland country.
And he sent the blessed David to the desert of Gareja, and others to the area around our city.
And they went forth and settled, some in rocky cliffs and some in caves and holes in the ground.
And Isidore settled in the cliff of Samtavisi. So they parted from one another and became recluses, as it pleased the Holy Spirit.
And the faithful of Christ would come to those holy elders. Instructed by them and built up in spirit, they would go back to their own homes.
And by the help of God they worked great healings and strengthened the faithful.
Now the holy father John had brought relics of the holy martyrs from his own country.
And when he sent out his disciples, he gave them some of those relics, so that by their grace they might be guarded against all the snares of the devil.
And he also kept some with himself, so that he might always look upon them, and at all times share in their martyrdom in his mind, and have them as a consolation for soul and body.
And he also had one disciple with him, who was a comfort to him. And his prayer rose up, purified the air and passed through the ether.
But those demons who hate the good, who had dwelt there from the beginning, could not endure the prayer of our father John, for it pierced them like arrows.
One day they roused themselves, fell upon holy John and began to fight against him with many different schemes. They surrounded him, stirred up a commotion and said to him:
"Who are you, or where do you come from? This place is ours, and if you do not leave here, we will bring great and astonishing trials upon you."
But he sealed himself with the cross of Christ and said: "Look, here I am. If you have received permission from Christ,
do whatever you wish. For I am a servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, and I am not afraid of your snares."
Then the chief of the demons called him by name: "John, John, why have you wronged us, and where did you come here from?
Now go away from here, for this place is ours and you cannot live with us. And if you do not listen to me,
you will destroy yourself, for you cannot stand against this multitude of ours that you see. Go away, and do not deceive yourself."
But holy John answered: "You never want a good purpose for our race, for you are wicked, treacherous, liars and vain. So how should I listen to you?
"I know all this thoroughly: you do not want good for human beings. And what claim do you have to this place?
For the heavens and the earth were made by our God, and he created them as a place of rest for us, his servants!
But for you he has prepared the outer darkness and the unquenchable fire, in which you are to be punished forever: you, all your helpers, and all who follow your will.
"And are you not the one who took the paradise of delight from us? For you devised a scheme and lured our father Adam out of paradise, and by your trickery we were handed over to death.
But the sweet and good-loving God again had mercy on the one created in his image, and the one whom you had brought to dishonour and who was buried in the depths
of hell he mercifully raised up again, brought up and granted the kingdom. And that which you deceitfully promised him when you said to him,
'You will be given divinity,' behold, we have now received through our Lord Jesus Christ.
And now, behold, you are driven out on every side by the children of Adam, and there is no place for you except that outer darkness, for you yourself hated the light and loved the darkness.
For you were an angel, but you became arrogant and fell because of your wickedness.
Now, by the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, flee from this mountain, for Christ has granted this to me."
When holy John had said all this to him, all those demons let out a cry of lamentation and woe, and said:
"Oh! By the invoking of the name of Jesus we are driven out of every place, and he gives power to all
who follow him. Woe, woe! Let us go away to the innermost lands of the pagans and settle there."
And at once they came out of the mountain like a thick mist, headed toward the north and vanished.
When all who lived around that mountain heard of this, which God had done through the prayer of our holy father John,
they all gave glory to God, because they knew the wickedness of those demons who had settled on that mountain. And they said:
"Truly God does the will of those who fear him."
And the blessed elder stayed on that mountain and was eager to store up good works, so that he would not appear before his Lord empty-handed.
And he began to fast and pray strictly, so that he could offer good works to the Lord.

The mountain had formerly been without water, and holy John saw the hard labour and sweat of his disciple, who used to carry water up from the foot of the mountain and bring it to the elder for his needs.
He took pity on him and with tears begged God to make water spring up on that high ridge.
In ancient times God gave water to Israel in the wilderness through his servant Moses: water came out of the dry rock, and he satisfied the twelve tribes.
That same good God heard the prayer of the holy elder and made sweet, cool water spring up from the dry ground on that mountain,
and it flows to this day, to the glory of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
And when this miracle happened, those who lived around that mountain spread the news of it.
Because everyone knew that there had been no water at all on that mountain, people came from every side.
And they brought the sick, and when they drank the water and anointed themselves with it, they were all healed. Even to this day, those who come in faith benefit from it.
But he did not want to build on that place. Instead, he chose to live alone, for he found a small cave there, and in it he completed his life as an ascetic stranger to the world.
And he lived "afflicted and ill-treated, of whom this world was not worthy."
And through the miracles he worked, he shone out like the morning star.
And his fame spread through the land of Kartli, for it is not possible that someone who has lit a lamp should put it under a bushel,
but rather on a lampstand, so that it may give light to people. Even though he wished to hide himself,
he still could not hide, just as when a perfumer fills a flask [?] with ointment, puts it inside another vessel, seals it, and thinks he has hidden it.
But the fragrance of the ointment reaches those who come near. In this way God glorified him, and God was also glorified through him.
One day his disciple went to the spring to draw water, and a great bear was standing over it.
He was afraid, turned back, and told the elder. The elder went and said to the bear: "If you have not drunk, drink and go away.
And I tell you: from now on do not harm any human being when a person meets you on this mountain." And so it has remained until now: no bear harms anyone at all.
When the elder said this to the bear, it obeyed like a servant and went away quietly with its head bowed.
O brothers who are listening, consider now the wonder and glory of God,
for just as long ago Daniel tamed the beasts in the pit because of his fasting, which he kept for the sake of the divine law,
never touching the food of the Chaldeans, so too through the prayer of this holy father of ours the beasts of his mountain became gentle and harmless.
But this makes me ashamed: creatures of a bestial and speechless nature heard his words, and now their offspring and their offspring's offspring carry out the command of the holy father John,
while we have shown ourselves more wicked than wild beasts and dumb animals,

for day after day we read about what happened in the past and we hear the commandments that have been given, yet we do not stop harming our neighbours. We abstain from eating meat, yet we chew on the flesh of our neighbours.
We have received the commandment to love one another, but we have neglected that command of the Lord. Know that we are liable to judgement.

Let us be watchful from now on, my brothers. Let us be watchful and cast away from us envy, quarrelling and the plotting of evil against our neighbour. Let us root out all wickedness and live in a way that pleases God, so that we may not be condemned for eternity.
But I was speaking of the earlier matter.
Once a man was brought on a bed to this holy father of ours John. He was bent and paralysed, and all his limbs were loosened.
They brought him in before him and pleaded with holy [?] John:
"Have mercy, holy one of God, on this paralysed man, for we believe that you are able to heal him by the power of Christ."
And the paralysed man also cried out: "Have mercy on me, servant of God, on this unburied dead man, and grant me a little grace so that I may be healed."
Although this task seemed heavy to blessed John, he remembered the saying of Paul, who says:
"You who are strong, bear the weak [?]." For this reason he also said to him:
"Our Lord Jesus Christ heals you." At that very moment he stood up on his feet, and his paralysed limbs were healed at once.
Those who saw it gave thanks to God and to holy John.
Another time they brought a man possessed by a demon, who was so badly tormented that he could not even speak. John saw him and had pity on him.
Saint John answered and said to it: "Evil spirit, why do you torment this man? For the place given to you is the desert and the waterless land.
I tell you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: come out of this man!"
And it went out at his command. The man was healed, and everyone was amazed. The elder said to them:
"Why are you amazed? I am not a physician. It is by calling on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ that every sickness and every power of darkness flees.
For he himself said: 'Whoever believes in me will also do what I do, and will do greater things than I.'"
We have written down these few out of his many great deeds, because time is short.
But these are enough to give a taste of that God-clothed man. Just as with a great river, a single cup shows
what taste it has, so it is with blessed John, for anyone who wishes. But the miracles that our holy John performed are many.
Now let us speak of his blessed disciples, who were enlightened by divine grace, who enlightened others as well and built monasteries,
which stand to this day and where healings take place. We are not able to tell about each of them one by one.
One of the disciples, named Tata, built a monastery below, at the foot of that mountain,
in which the monks multiplied and lived in complete good order. We will remember the others after this, and let us glorify God, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
